title: VPC Satellite Staging and Operator Packaging Playbook
author: Marina Solis
body:
Summary:
This playbook describes a repeatable, low-risk process for commissioning VPC-connected satellite (edge) nodes that run a Private Redwood runtime, packaging and signing the operator images used for on-prem field installs, and executing a staged rollout with clear day‑2 operational contracts. It is intended for SRE/Platform engineers and operator field teams responsible for multi‑site private deployments and integrates packaging, observability, upgrade, and rollback guidance into a single operational flow.

When to use this playbook:
- New customer requiring geographically distributed VPC satellite nodes (e.g., branch offices, edge sites)
- Customers that require signed operator images and an evidence trail for audits
- Rollouts where minimizing tenant impact and achieving zero data loss are priorities

Primary owners and contacts:
- Document owner: Platform Reliability (owner_team: engineering)
- Runbook contact: SRE Oncall rota (pager: #sre-private-deploy)
- Packaging owner: Build & Image team (lead: Jin Park)
- Field operator lead: Customer Success Ops (lead: Omar Reyes)

Goals and SLOs for satellite launches:
- Target: <150 ms p50 inference latency for pinned small models at 512 tokens (customer SLA dependent)
- Availability SLO: 99.95% for control-plane reachability within region for 30-day windows
- Observability coverage: 100% of traffic routes instrumented; key traces sampled at 5%

Prerequisites checklist (operator + customer):
1) Customer VPC connectivity: BGP/peering configured, CIDR allocation produced, egress rules documented.
2) KMS/HSM access: customer KMS endpoints reachable and service account configured.
3) Hardware & firmware: NVIDIA driver >= 535.x (or vendor equivalent), BIOS firmware matching approved list; GPU thermal policy tested.
4) Image signing policy: build pipeline okta token and signing key present in secure key vault.
5) Telemetry endpoints: telemetry proxy URL, sampling policy, and retention contract defined.

Staging topology and phases:
- Phase 1: Canary site (single satellite) — no customer traffic, synthetic load only.
- Phase 2: Pilot sites (2–3 satellites) — limited customer traffic (5–10% modal split).
- Phase 3: Regional roll (N sites) — full traffic gradually shifted via weight-based routing.
Each site runs the same runtime operator but may use model-variant pinning and runtime knobs to match local capacity.

Staged rollout matrix (operator-controlled knobs):
| Phase | Max sites | Traffic share | KV cache policy | Batching multiplier | Fallback model | Rollback trigger |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Canary | 1 | 0% | disabled | 1x | none | control-plane error rate >3% or tail latency >500ms |
| Pilot | 3 | 5–10% | prefix-only | 1–2x | quantized-variant | error budget burn >20% in 12h |
| Regional | variable | incremental to 100% | full | 2–4x | regional-fallback | sustained SLA breach 1h or operator manual stop |

Packaging and image verification (operator build steps):
1) Build images in isolated CI pipeline (project: private-packaging).
2) Run image hardening scripts: remove debug bins, validate TLS ciphers, set non-root user.
3) Sign images with customer escrowed signing key using cosign: cosign sign --key k8s-signer.key registry.example.com/redwood/operator:sha256-XYZ.
4) Produce SBOM and attestation artifact (CycloneDX + provenance).
5) Push artifacts to customer approved registry and record digest in the deployment evidence bundle.
Important checks: image digest must match on operator manifest, SBOM must not include unapproved licenses, attestation must include build pipeline run id.

Operator manifest binding example (described):
- Use manifest patches to pin operator image: image: registry.example.com/redwood/operator@sha256:XYZ
- Set rolloutStrategy: "Canary" with maxUnavailable: 1 and progressDeadlineSeconds: 1800
- Enable liveness/readiness probes with backoffLimit 6

Upgrade and rollback procedure (operator-level, step-by-step):
1) Prepare image + evidence bundle and stage in pre-prod registry.
2) Execute dry-run apply to canary site: kubectl apply --server-dry-run -f operator-canary.yaml; validate events.
3) Deploy to Canary with 0% traffic shift. Run smoke tests for 30 minutes (health checks, synthetic inference).
4) Observe metrics for 2 hours: latency, error rate, KV hit ratio, GPU utilization.
5) If pass, advance to Pilot (5–10% traffic) using routing weight change. Monitor 24h.
6) If any metric crosses the rollback trigger, perform immediate rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/operator -n redwood-system --to-revision=<previous>.
7) Collect forensic evidence and create rollback packet: kernel logs, operator events, telemetry windows (T-30m to T+30m).
Notes on safe rollback: avoid simultaneous cache migrations during rollout. If rollforward required, use staged config gate to enable feature flags.

Day‑2 operations and observability contract (operator ↔ customer):
- Logging: control-plane and runtime logs forwarded to customer endpoint with 7d retention by default, 30d optional.
- Metrics: key metrics (rpc_latencies_p50/p95, kv_cache_hits, gpu_mem_free) exported at 10s resolution with 5% trace sampling.
- Alerting thresholds (default recommended):
  - control-plane-http-5xx-rate > 1% sustained 10m -> P1
  - inference-tail-latency95 > 600ms -> P1
  - gpu-temp > 85C for >2m -> P0
  - kv-cache-miss-rate > 40% for 30m -> P2
- Oncall playbook excerpts:
  1) For P1: Activate cross-team incident bridge, flip regional traffic to fallback model, and apply operator safemode (scale to 0 safe pods if necessary).
  2) For P0 (hardware): instruct field operator to perform immediate GPU power cycling and thermal diagnostics per hardware vendor checklist.

Customer readiness checklist (package to deliver to customer before pilot):
- Completed: BGP peering test with RTT < 50ms to control-plane proxy (for regional launches).
- Completed: KMS test with key create/rotate cycle within policy.
- Completed: Signed operator image digest and SBOM delivered with checksum.
- Completed: Telemetry endpoint and sampling policy agreed and firewall exemptions configured.
- Completed: Field operator contact and escalation matrix with 24/7 phone coverage during pilot.

Common failure modes and mitigation recipes:
- Symptom: High tail latency after pilot traffic shift.
  - Likely causes: high KV miss rate, GPU throttling, or ineffective batching.
  - Mitigation: Reduce batching multiplier, enable prefix caching, or shift traffic back to hosted fallback.
- Symptom: Image verification mismatch on customer registry.
  - Mitigation: Re-fetch digest, validate cosign attestation, and re-push signed image; gate operator deployment until digest matches.

Appendix: sample CLI snippets and pseudo-manifests
- Sign image: cosign sign --key /secrets/customer-signer.key registry.customer.example/redwood/operator:1.4.0
- Evidence bundle (example fields): build_id=ci-2026-0423, digest=sha256:XYZ, sbom_url=https://artifact-store/acme/operator/sbom.json
- Routing weight change via control-plane API (curl example): curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/route-shift -d '{"satellite_id":"sat-123","weight":5}'
